answer: An agent claiming a harbor berth locks a 70-credit bond and pays a 30-credit cover premium for vine cargo. The harbor auditor posts it on a vine manifest and checks its ledge tally against the declaration; a mismatch burns the bond and voids the cover. The k-th fake identity pays 100 credits plus 2 for each earlier claim, so the 1,000th pays 2,098 and 1,000 fakes cost 1,099,000 credits. A rented-manifest ring fails because each manifest is key-bound to one berth and one tide window and the auditor recounts the ledge tally. An honest agent pays 100 once and keeps its cover.
